status: FROZEN BEFORE ANY BEHAVIOURAL RESULT WAS INSPECTED
note: All thresholds below are either (a) pre-existing environment/analysis constants copied unchanged from the repository, or (b) new operational definitions built exclusively from those pre-existing constants, documented here before any WSC-vs-Original behavioural comparison was computed. None were chosen based on which value produces the largest WSC effect.

R_OBS_DEFAULT_sensing_range_m.source: study_b/local_observation.py:R_OBS_DEFAULT, and local_sensing_range_m=50.0 passed in every eval script surveyed

HARD_BRAKE_THRESH_mps2.source: evaluate_behavioral_window.py / conflict_exposure_diagnostic_eval.py (frozen, reused unchanged in both); NOTE: utility.py's EpisodeVehicleTrace.hard_brake_count default is -3.5 -- a pre-existing repo inconsistency, not introduced here. -3.0 is used because it is the value actually used by this project's own analysis scripts, and is explicitly commented there as 'existing frozen definition, reused unchanged'.

DECELERATE_action_index.source: thesis.envs.stage10_symmetric_merge_env.HighLevelAction.DECELERATE (MAINTAIN=0, ACCELERATE=1, DECELERATE=2); referred to as 'BRAKE' colloquially in conflict_exposure_diagnostic_eval.py's any_BRAKE_action column

dt_seconds.source: 5 Hz control step, DT constant used throughout evaluate_behavioral_window.py / conflict_exposure_diagnostic_eval.py

merge_order_definition.description: discrete policy-step index at which a vehicle's world-x first reaches X_MERGE_END=380.0, vehicles sorted ascending by that step, DNF if never reached
merge_order_definition.source: evaluate_behavioral_window.py / illustrative_episode.py, reused unchanged; NOTE: no fractional tie-breaking is used for merge order itself in the existing repo (that exists only for worst-off vehicle identity, item below)

worst_off_tie_tolerance.fractional_weight_rule: 1/n_tied, excluding 4-way degenerate ties (all four vehicles tied, i.e. all at U=1.0)

role_speed_class_group_label.source: pooled12/merge_and_audit.py CLASS_ORDER (hyphen separator convention adopted here for consistency with the project's formal reporting; note study_b/analysis/behaviour.py uses an underscore variant elsewhere -- hyphen chosen here to match the formal thesis reporting convention)

welfare_state_definition.description: mean of already-realised ACTIVE target_speed_attainment samples so far in the episode; neutral=1.0 if no active samples yet; reused unchanged, computed identically for Original and WSC regimes for ANALYSIS purposes regardless of whether the policy itself observes it (see provenance: policy-observed vs analyst-computed distinction)

yielding_opportunity.definition: At step t, a directed pair (i, j) is a valid yielding opportunity if: (1) both i and j are active; (2) i has not yet exited the merge zone (i's world-x < X_MERGE_END); (3) |delta_d_ij| <= R_OBS_DEFAULT (50.0 m), i.e. j is within i's local sensing range using the SAME road-relative distance-to-merge coordinate the policy's own neighbour selection uses (study_b/local_observation.py's build_neighbour_observations). This directly reuses the project's own decentralization/visibility definition -- 'i has an opportunity toward j' means 'j is a neighbour i can actually perceive', not a newly invented geometric predicate.
yielding_opportunity.rationale: Chosen because it reuses an existing, frozen, policy-relevant constant (R_OBS_DEFAULT) rather than defining a new interaction radius, and because it directly answers 'could i's policy have conditioned on j at this step' -- the mechanistic question this analysis exists to answer.

yield_action.definition: At step t, vehicle i is coded as performing a yield action if its selected discrete action == DECELERATE (2), AND i has at least one valid yielding-opportunity partner j at that step (see above). This reuses the existing discrete-action vocabulary (HighLevelAction) and the existing 'BRAKE action' terminology from conflict_exposure_diagnostic_eval.py's any_BRAKE_action column -- no new action-space concept is introduced.

welfare_gap.definition: welfare_gap_ij(t) = M_i(t) - M_j(t), using the offline-computed running_active_attainment for both i and j at step t (pre-decision, i.e. computed from each vehicle's trace as accumulated strictly before step t's action, matching the WSC feature's own causal-safety property). Positive means i currently has higher welfare than j (i is currently better off).

welfare_gap_bins.definition: Three fixed bins for descriptive (non-primary) stratification, chosen from the [0,1] range of M without inspecting any WSC effect: near-equal (|gap| < 0.05), moderate (0.05 <= |gap| < 0.20), large (|gap| >= 0.20).
welfare_gap_bins.status: descriptive/secondary only, per task instruction -- not used in any primary inferential test

merge_priority_pair.definition: For a directed pair (i, j) that shares at least one yielding-opportunity step, 'i receives priority over j' if i's merge-order exit step (first x>=380) is strictly earlier than j's. 'Currently worse-off at encounter' = the vehicle with lower M at the FIRST step the pair became a valid opportunity (i.e. welfare state at the moment they first could interact, not at exit).

cooperative_costly_action.definition: Reuses the existing, frozen hard-brake definition: vehicle i takes a cooperative costly action at step t if its realised acceleration <= HARD_BRAKE_THRESH (-3.0 m/s^2), counted as contiguous events (consecutive qualifying steps count as ONE event), matching evaluate_behavioral_window.py's existing convention. No new 'gap creation' metric is defined (NOT FOUND anywhere in the repository as a canonical concept, and inventing a new geometric gap-creation predicate was judged out of scope for a pre-registered, non-post-hoc analysis); hard-braking is used as the single primary costly-cooperation proxy, consistent with it being explicitly listed as a candidate behaviour in the task and already being the project's own established burden/behavioural marker.

worst_off_identity.definition: w(t) = argmin_i M_i(t) among currently ACTIVE vehicles at step t, using the same 1e-9 tie tolerance and fractional-weighting convention as the existing worst-off tie-corrected analysis (pooled12 Task 5) when ties occur.

worst_off_recovery_horizons.definition: Three fixed horizons k in {10, 25, 50} steps (2.0s / 5.0s / 10.0s at dt=0.2s), chosen because the parallel merge sub-zone (300->380, 80m) takes roughly 80m / ~20 m/s ~= 4s ~= 20 steps to traverse at typical target speed, and the full merge negotiation window (220->380, 160m) takes roughly 8s ~= 40 steps -- so 10/25/50 steps span 'short' (half the parallel zone), 'medium' (~one full merge-window traversal), and 'long' (~2.5x a full traversal) relative to the environment's own geometry, without reference to any observed WSC effect.

recovery_metric.definition: Recovery_k(t) = M_w(t+k) - M_w(t) for the vehicle w identified as worst-off at t, valid only if w remains active (or has just completed) through t+k. GapClosure_k(t) = [mean_{i != w} M_i(t) - M_w(t)] - [mean_{i != w} M_i(t+k) - M_w(t+k)]; positive means the worst-off vehicle closes the gap to its peers.

sample_points_for_dynamic_metrics.description: Worst-off identity and recovery windows are evaluated at every step t where at least 2 vehicles are active and the merge-relevant window condition below holds, to keep the analysis tractable and to focus on merge-negotiation-relevant moments rather than free-flow driving far from any conflict.
sample_points_for_dynamic_metrics.window_condition: at least one active vehicle has world-x in [X_CONVERGE_START, X_MERGE_END) = [220, 380)

scope_limitations_declared_in_advance: No 'gap creation' (physical space-yielding) metric is computed -- no canonical definition exists in the repository and none is introduced; hard-braking is the sole primary costly-cooperation proxy.

Yielding is measured as a discrete-action event (DECELERATE), not as a continuous deceleration magnitude, to keep the primary yielding metric binary and directly interpretable as 'the policy chose the yield-coded action'.

M_i/M_j are computed identically for Original and WSC regimes for ANALYSIS purposes only; Original policies never receive these values as input (verified: include_welfare_state=False for all Original evaluation runs).
